objectives: To develop basic understanding of optics and wave nature of light.
To elaborate interference, diffraction, polarization of light, principles of lasers and optical fibres.
To apply optics concepts to solve related real world physics problems.
To demonstrate various optics based experimental techniques.

outcomes.statement: Outline the basic concepts of light and its properties
Categorize optical phenomena, such as interference, diffraction, polarization, coherent light sources and propagation through optical fibres
Apply theories to solve optics problems and perform optics-based experiments
Analyze optics based theoretical and experimental results.

syllabus.title: Interference
syllabus.topics: Foundational concepts on Interference, phase change on reflection: Stokes’ treatment, Lloyd’s mirror, Cosine law, interference in thin films: parallel and wedge-shaped films, Newton’s rings--measurement of wavelength and refractive index, Michelson’s Interferometer.

syllabus.title: Diffraction
syllabus.topics: Diffraction, superposition of n simple harmonic waves (equal phase difference), Fraunhofer diffraction, intensity distribution – single slit, double slit- and N-slit (diffraction grating) – intensity distribution, determination of wavelength, absent spectra (missing orders) in grating, dispersive power of a grating, resolving power of a grating, Fresnel’s diffraction, Fresnel’s assumptions, Fresnel’s half-period zones for plane wave, wave theory of zone plate: multiple focii, of a zone plate

syllabus.title: Polarization
syllabus.topics: Polarization of light, Brewster’s law, Malus’s law, Double refraction in Calcite crystal, Nicol’s prism, Huygen’s theory of double refraction, Quarter wave plate, half wave plate, Elliptically and circularly polarized light-Analysis, production and conversion, Babinet’s compensator-analysis of elliptically polarized light, optical activity, specific rotation, Fresnel’s theory of optical rotation, Laurent’s half-shade polarimeter, Biquartz polarimeter

syllabus.title: Lasers & Fiber Optics
syllabus.topics: Introduction, Spontaneous and Stimulated emission of radiation, Relation b/w Einstein’s A and B coefficients, Population inversion & types of pumping, Main components of a Laser, Construction & working of Ruby Laser and its applications, Construction & working of Helium-Neon laser and its applications. Fundamental ideas about optical fiber, Numerical aperture, Acceptance angle and cone, Attenuation and losses, Types of fibers, propagation mechanism and communication in optical fiber.
